featured_techniques.technique: Dual overhead cam (DOHC) cam timing overview
Valve train operation and lifter types comparison
Piston, rings, and combustion chamber overview

sections.description: EricTheCarGuy introduces the video focus: identifying and naming the basic engine parts, with a quick note on the engine vs motor terminology and the specific 1.8L Honda Integra reference.
sections.title: Introduction and scope

sections.description: Explanation of a dual overhead cam engine, including the roles of the intake and exhaust camshafts, cam lobes, and how they regulate valve opening and timing to enable engine breathing.
sections.title: DOHC architecture and cam function

sections.description: Discussion of cam followers, valve lifters, and the difference between hydraulic and solid lifters, as well as a comparison between pushrod and overhead-cam configurations.
sections.title: Valve train dynamics and lifter types

sections.description: Overview of the old-school distributor, its mechanical linkage to the camshaft, and how the oil pump is driven in many engines, highlighting potential timing issues when components are out of time.
sections.title: Ignition timing and oil system connections

sections.description: Description of the intake and exhaust manifolds, how runners feed each cylinder, and the importance of equal-length runners for smooth operation and balanced power.
sections.title: intake and exhaust manifolds; runners

sections.description: Comparison of fuel delivery in injected vs carbureted systems, including the placement of injectors behind the fuel rail and timing with the engine's sensors.
sections.title: Fuel delivery: injectors, rails, and air/fuel flow

sections.description: Exploration of cylinder head features, including the head gasket, valve seats, guides, seals, and the impact of combustion chamber geometry on engine performance.
sections.title: Cylinder head, combustion chamber, and valve machining

sections.description: Discussion on valve springs, retainers, and keepers, and how spring strength relates to RPM and valve control, including the phenomenon of valve float.
sections.title: Valve train retention and behavior under RPM

sections.description: Coverage of the crankshaft and its attachments, including flywheel vs flex plate depending on transmission type, and the function of the harmonic balancer to smooth out torsional pulses.
sections.title: Crankshaft assembly, damping, and engine balance

sections.description: Close with a piston-centric view: the rings, wrist pin, and connecting rod interaction, how displacement is defined, and a candid note on the engine's overall efficiency versus power output.
sections.title: Pistons, rings, and overall engine efficiency

summary: In this instructional video, host EricTheCarGuy walks through the basic components and functions of a conventional internal combustion engine using a 1.8 liter Honda Integra engine as a visual reference. The talk covers terminology (engine vs. motor), major assemblies (valve train, camshafts, timing system, ignition, intake/exhaust manifolds), and critical subsystems (valves, springs, seals, pistons, rings, crankshaft, oiling system, and cooling-related components). The video emphasizes how timing and geometry affect engine breathing, torque, and horsepower, and it includes practical anecdotes about common designs (DOHC, distributor ignition, carbureted vs. fuel-injected layouts) and the trade-offs engineers balance in automotive design.
title: Dissecting an Engine: Basic Parts and Their Functions (Honda 1.8L DOHC)
